faqs.question: How do I resize an image?
faqs.answer: Upload an image, then either pick a social media preset or enter a custom width and height in pixels. You can also scale by percentage. Maintain aspect ratio keeps the proportions intact so your image isn't stretched.

faqs.question: Which formats are supported?
faqs.answer: You can upload JPG, PNG, WebP, and other common image formats. The resized result is downloaded as a PNG by default, which preserves quality and transparency.

faqs.question: What are the social media presets for?
faqs.answer: Presets apply the exact pixel dimensions recommended for Instagram posts (1080x1080), stories (1080x1920), YouTube thumbnails (1280x720), Facebook covers, and more — so you don't have to look up the numbers yourself.

faqs.question: Will enlarging a small image make it blurry?
faqs.answer: Enlarging an image interpolates new pixels, so the result can look softer or blurry. For best quality, resize images that are already at least as large as the target dimensions.

intro.title: What Is the Image Resizer?
paragraphs: The Image Resizer lets you change the width and height of an image to exact pixel values, percentages, or popular social media presets. A live preview updates as you adjust the settings, so you can confirm the result before downloading.
All resizing happens in your browser. Images are never uploaded, which keeps the tool fast, free, and private.

sections.title: How to Resize an Image

metadata.title: Chmod Calculator
metadata.description: Calculate Unix file permissions visually using chmod

faqs.question: What is chmod?
faqs.answer: chmod is a command in Unix and Unix-like systems (such as Linux and macOS) used to change the permissions of files or directories. Permissions determine who can read, write or execute a file.

faqs.question: How do permissions work?
faqs.answer: Permissions are grouped into three classes: owner, group and others. Each class can have read (r, value 4), write (w, value 2) and execute (x, value 1) permissions. These values are added together to get the numeric representation (like 755).

faqs.question: How do I use the chmod calculator?
faqs.answer: Click the permission checkboxes to set the desired permissions for owner, group and others. The calculator shows the numeric and symbolic representations in real time.

faqs.question: What is the difference between numeric and symbolic representations?
faqs.answer: The numeric representation uses three digits (like 755), where each digit is the sum of the permission values. The symbolic representation uses letters (like rwxr-xr-x), where r means read, w means write, x means execute and - means no permission.

faqs.question: What are common permission settings?
faqs.answer: 755 (rwxr-xr-x) for directories and executable files, 644 (rw-r--r--) for regular files, 700 (rwx------) for private directories, and 600 (rw-------) for sensitive files.

faqs.question: Can I set special permissions?
faqs.answer: This calculator handles basic permissions. Special permissions (such as setuid, setgid and the sticky bit) require an additional fourth digit in the numeric representation.

faqs.question: What is a cron expression?
faqs.answer: A cron expression is a string used to schedule tasks on Unix-like systems. It consists of five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month and day of week. Each field can contain specific values, ranges, lists or wildcards.

faqs.question: How do I build a cron expression?
faqs.answer: Use the presets to quickly pick common schedules, or enter a value for each field manually. The tool shows the expression in English and displays the next run times.

faqs.question: What are the fields of a cron expression?
faqs.answer: A standard cron expression has five fields: minute (0-59), hour (0-23), day of month (1-31), month (1-12) and day of week (0-7, where both 0 and 7 are Sunday).

faqs.question: What does * mean in cron?
faqs.answer: The asterisk (*) means "every" or "all". It matches every possible value for a field, meaning the task runs at every value of that field.

faqs.question: How do I specify multiple values?
faqs.answer: Use commas to separate values (like 1,3,5), hyphens for ranges (like 1-5), or step values (like */5 meaning every 5 units).

faqs.question: Are cron expressions safe?
faqs.answer: Yes. This tool generates cron expressions locally in the browser. No data is sent to any server.

faqs.question: What is CSS minification?
faqs.answer: CSS minification reduces the size of a CSS file by removing unnecessary whitespace, comments and other characters. This can improve page load speed and reduce bandwidth usage.

faqs.question: How do I minify CSS?
faqs.answer: Paste your CSS code into the input field. Click the minify button. The tool removes whitespace and comments to produce a smaller output. Copy the result or download the minified file.

faqs.question: Does minification affect CSS functionality?
faqs.answer: No. Minification only removes characters that are unnecessary for rendering. The functionality of your CSS remains unchanged. However, it may make the code harder to read or debug.

faqs.question: How much can minification reduce file size?
faqs.answer: The reduction depends on the original CSS. Files with lots of whitespace and comments can be reduced by 50-80%. Already compact CSS may see only a small reduction.

faqs.question: Is my CSS sent to a server?
faqs.answer: No. All minification happens locally in your browser. The code never leaves your device.

faqs.question: Can I minify large CSS files?
faqs.answer: Yes. Since minification happens in the browser, it can handle large CSS files. However, very large files (>50 MB) may be slow due to browser memory limits.

faqs.question: What is a hash generator?
faqs.answer: A hash generator is a tool that converts input text into a fixed-length string. Hashes are one-way — you cannot reverse a hash back into the original text. They are used for data integrity, password storage and digital signatures.

faqs.question: Which hash algorithms are supported?
faqs.answer: The tool supports SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512. SHA-256 and SHA-512 are recommended for secure applications. SHA-1 is no longer recommended for security reasons but may be used for legacy systems.

faqs.question: How do I generate a hash?
faqs.answer: Type or paste text into the input field. Select the desired hash algorithm. The hash is generated and displayed immediately. Click copy to copy it to your clipboard.

faqs.question: Are the hashes secure?
faqs.answer: SHA-256 and SHA-512 are currently considered secure. SHA-1 has known collision vulnerabilities and should not be used for security purposes. For password hashing, use dedicated functions such as bcrypt or Argon2.

faqs.question: Can I hash files?
faqs.answer: The current version only supports text input. For file hashing, you need to read the file contents and pass them as text.

faqs.question: Is hashing safe in the browser?
faqs.answer: Yes. All hashing is done in the browser using the native Web Crypto API. No data is sent to any server.

faqs.answer: HTML entities are codes used to display reserved characters or characters that are not easy to type on a keyboard in HTML. For example, < becomes <, > becomes >, and & becomes &.

faqs.question: How do I encode HTML entities?
faqs.answer: Paste your text into the input field. Select the encode mode. The tool converts special characters into HTML entities.

faqs.question: How do I decode HTML entities?

faqs.question: Why do I need to encode HTML entities?

faqs.question: What is the difference between named and numeric entities?
faqs.answer: Named entities use names (like <), while numeric entities use character codes (like <). They are equivalent, but named entities are easier to read.

faqs.question: Is HTML entity encoding safe?

faqs.question: What is HTML minification?
faqs.answer: HTML minification reduces the size of an HTML file by removing unnecessary whitespace, comments and optionally inlining CSS/JavaScript. This can improve page load speed and reduce bandwidth usage.

faqs.question: How do I minify HTML?
faqs.answer: Paste your HTML code into the input field. Click the minify button. The tool removes whitespace and comments to produce a smaller output. Copy the result or download the minified file.

faqs.question: Does minification affect HTML functionality?
faqs.answer: No. Minification only removes characters that are unnecessary for rendering. The functionality and appearance of your HTML remain unchanged. However, it may make the code harder to read or debug.

faqs.question: How much can minification reduce file size?
faqs.answer: The reduction depends on the original HTML. Files with lots of whitespace and comments can be reduced by 50-80%. Already compact HTML may see only a small reduction.

faqs.question: Is my HTML sent to a server?
faqs.answer: No. All minification happens locally in your browser. The code never leaves your device.

faqs.question: Can I minify large HTML files?
faqs.answer: Yes. Since minification happens in the browser, it can handle large HTML files. However, very large files (>50 MB) may be slow due to browser memory limits.

metadata.title: JWT Decoder
metadata.description: Decode and inspect JSON Web Tokens (JWT), with signature verification support

faqs.question: What is a JWT?
faqs.answer: A JWT (JSON Web Token) is a compact, URL-safe format for representing claims between parties. It consists of three parts — header, payload and signature — encoded in Base64URL and separated by dots (.).

faqs.question: How do I decode a JWT?
faqs.answer: Paste the JWT into the input field. The tool decodes it automatically and displays the header and payload parts in a readable format. It also checks whether the token has expired.

faqs.question: Can this tool verify JWT signatures?
faqs.answer: No. This tool only decodes JWTs without verifying the signature. Verification requires the key used to sign the token. Always verify JWTs on the server side.

faqs.question: Are JWTs secure?
faqs.answer: JWTs can be used securely, but must be implemented correctly. Always verify the signature, check the expiration time, do not store sensitive data in the payload (it is Base64 encoded, not encrypted), and use HTTPS in transit.

faqs.question: What are common use cases for JWTs?
faqs.answer: JWTs are commonly used for authentication (after login, the server returns a JWT that the client stores), information exchange (securely transferring information between parties) and authorization (representing user permissions).

faqs.question: Is decoding a JWT safe?
faqs.answer: Yes. This tool decodes JWTs locally in the browser. No data is sent to any server. However, do not store sensitive information in client-side JWTs, because anyone can decode them.

faqs.answer: Meta tags are tags in the head of an HTML document that provide metadata about the page, such as the title, description, keywords and Open Graph information. They are not displayed on the page but are used by search engines and social media platforms.

faqs.question: What are Open Graph tags?
faqs.answer: Open Graph tags control how your page appears when shared on Facebook, LinkedIn and other social platforms. They define the title, description, image and other elements shown when sharing.

faqs.question: What are Twitter card tags?
faqs.answer: Twitter card tags control how your page appears when shared on Twitter. They are similar to Open Graph tags but specific to Twitter, and can enable special formats such as large images or app install cards.

faqs.question: Are meta tags important for SEO?

faqs.question: What is robots.txt?
faqs.answer: robots.txt is a text file placed in the root directory of a website. It tells search engine crawlers which pages or files may or may not be crawled on your website.

faqs.question: How do I use the robots.txt generator?
faqs.answer: Select the crawlers to allow (such as Googlebot, Bingbot), add allow and disallow rules, and specify the sitemap location. The tool generates a robots.txt file for you to download or copy.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Disallow and Allow directives?
faqs.answer: Disallow tells crawlers not to access specific paths. Allow overrides Disallow and permits access to specific sub-paths. By default, everything is allowed if no rules are specified.

faqs.question: Should I block all crawlers?
faqs.answer: Usually not. You generally only want to block specific directories (like /admin/ or /private/). Blocking all crawlers (User-agent: * Disallow: /) removes your website from search results.

faqs.question: Can robots.txt protect sensitive pages?
faqs.answer: No. robots.txt is publicly accessible and anyone can read it. It does not prevent users from accessing pages. For real protection, use password protection or server-side authentication.

faqs.question: Should I include a Sitemap directive?
faqs.answer: Yes. Including Sitemap: https://example.com/sitemap.xml helps search engines find your sitemap and index your website better.

intro.title: What is a Robots.txt Generator?
paragraphs: A robots.txt generator is a free online tool for creating robots.txt files. It helps you control how search engine crawlers interact with your website, specify which paths are allowed or disallowed, and include sitemap references. All generation happens in the browser.

sections.title: How to create robots.txt
paragraphs: Select the crawler to configure (or use * for all crawlers). Add allow and disallow rules to specify which paths may or may not be crawled. Add your sitemap URL. Copy the generated robots.txt content and upload it to the root directory of your website.

sections.title: Understanding the syntax
paragraphs: robots.txt uses the User-agent directive to specify which crawler a rule applies to. The Disallow directive blocks access to paths. The Allow directive overrides Disallow. The Sitemap directive specifies the sitemap location.

faqs.answer: A Unix timestamp is the number of seconds elapsed since January 1, 1970 00:00:00 UTC (known as the "epoch"). It is a standard way to represent time in computer systems and programming.

faqs.question: How do I convert a timestamp to a date?
faqs.answer: Enter the Unix timestamp in the timestamp field. The tool instantly converts it to a human-readable date and time, displayed in your local timezone and UTC.

faqs.question: How do I convert a date to a timestamp?
faqs.answer: Pick a date and time with the date picker or enter it manually. The tool generates the corresponding Unix timestamp.

faqs.question: Are timestamps in seconds or milliseconds?
faqs.answer: The tool shows both second (10-digit) and millisecond (13-digit) timestamps. Most systems use seconds, but JavaScript's Date.now() returns milliseconds.

faqs.question: What is the current timestamp?
faqs.answer: The current timestamp is shown at the top of the tool and updates in real time every second. It displays the current Unix time in seconds and milliseconds.

faqs.question: How are timezones handled?
faqs.answer: Timestamps are always based on UTC. The converted date is displayed in both your local timezone and UTC for easy reference.

metadata.title: URL Encoder
metadata.description: Encode or decode URLs and query string parameters

faqs.question: What is URL encoding?
faqs.answer: URL encoding (also called percent-encoding) converts special characters into a format of % followed by two hexadecimal digits. For example, a space becomes %20. This is necessary to safely transmit characters in URLs.

faqs.question: How do I encode a URL?
faqs.answer: Paste the URL or text into the input field. Select the encode mode. The tool converts special characters into their percent-encoded equivalents.

faqs.question: How do I decode a URL?
faqs.answer: Paste the encoded URL into the input field. Select the decode mode. The tool converts percent-encoded characters back to their original format.

faqs.question: What is the difference between component encoding and full URI encoding?
faqs.answer: Component encoding (encodeURIComponent) encodes all characters except alphanumerics and -_.!~*'(). Full URI encoding (encodeURI) does not encode characters that are already valid in URLs, such as :/?#[]@.

faqs.question: Why is URL encoding needed?
faqs.answer: URLs can only use a subset of ASCII characters. URL encoding lets you safely include spaces, Unicode characters and special characters that could conflict with URL syntax.

faqs.question: Is URL encoding safe?
faqs.answer: Yes. This tool encodes and decodes URLs locally in the browser. No data is sent to any server.

intro.title: What is a URL Encoder/Decoder?

sections.title: Understanding the encoding modes
paragraphs: Component encoding (encodeURIComponent) encodes all characters except alphanumerics and a few special characters. Full URI encoding (encodeURI) preserves URL structure characters and only encodes characters that are not allowed in URLs.

faqs.question: What is BMI?
faqs.answer: Body Mass Index (BMI) is a measure of body fat based on height and weight. It's calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared. BMI is a screening tool, not a diagnostic measure of body fat or health.

faqs.question: What are the BMI categories?
faqs.answer: Underweight: below 18.5. Normal weight: 18.5-24.9. Overweight: 25.0-29.9. Obese: 30.0 and above. These categories are based on World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines for adults.

faqs.question: Is BMI accurate?
faqs.answer: BMI has limitations. It can't distinguish between muscle and fat mass, so muscular people may have a "high" BMI without having high body fat. It also doesn't account for age, sex, bone density, or fat distribution. Use it as one reference point, not a complete health picture.

faqs.question: Does BMI apply to children?
faqs.answer: For children, BMI uses age- and sex-specific percentiles rather than fixed adult categories. Pediatric BMI calculators account for normal growth patterns. This calculator is designed for adults (20+).

faqs.question: What is compound interest?
faqs.answer: Compound interest is interest calculated on both the initial principal and accumulated interest. Unlike simple interest, your earnings generate their own earnings, producing exponential growth over time.

faqs.question: How does compounding frequency affect returns?
faqs.answer: More frequent compounding (daily vs. annual) produces slightly higher returns because interest starts earning interest sooner. The difference is most noticeable with high rates and long time periods.

faqs.question: What is the Rule of 72?
faqs.answer: The Rule of 72 estimates how long it takes to double your money: divide 72 by the annual interest rate. At a 7% annual return, your money doubles roughly every 10.3 years (72 / 7 = 10.3).

faqs.question: Are the results guaranteed?
faqs.answer: No. This calculator assumes a fixed rate, which suits savings accounts and bonds. Investment returns (stocks, funds) vary year to year. Use average historical returns for long-term projections.

faqs.question: What is EXIF data?
faqs.answer: EXIF (Exchangeable Image File Format) is metadata stored in image files. It includes camera model, settings (aperture, shutter speed, ISO), date taken, GPS coordinates, and more.

faqs.question: How do I view EXIF data?

faqs.question: Do all images have EXIF data?
faqs.answer: No. EXIF data is typically added by digital cameras and smartphones. Images downloaded from the web or edited may have no EXIF data. Some formats (like PNG) don't support EXIF.

faqs.question: Does EXIF data include GPS location?
faqs.answer: It can. Many smartphones store GPS coordinates in EXIF data if camera location permissions are enabled on your device. You can view location data with this tool.

faqs.question: Can I remove EXIF data?
faqs.answer: This tool only views EXIF data, it doesn't remove it. To strip EXIF data, use a dedicated image editor or privacy tool.

faqs.question: How is the monthly mortgage payment calculated?
faqs.answer: The monthly payment is calculated using the standard amortization formula: M = P[r(1+r)^n]/[(1+r)^n - 1], where P is the loan amount, r is the monthly interest rate, and n is the total number of payments.

faqs.question: How accurate are the property tax and insurance estimates?
faqs.answer: Property tax rates are based on effective rates by state. Insurance rates are based on average annual premiums by state. Both are applied as a percentage of the home price and update automatically when you change state or price. These are state averages; actual costs vary by county, city, coverage level, and property specifics.

faqs.question: What is PMI?
faqs.answer: Private mortgage insurance (PMI) is required when your down payment is less than 20% of the home price. It typically costs 0.3%-1.5% of the loan amount per year and protects the lender in case of default.

faqs.question: Why do property taxes differ so much by state?
faqs.answer: Property tax rates range from 0.28% in Hawaii to 2.47% in New Jersey. That means on a $350,000 home you'd pay $980 per year in Hawaii and $8,645 in New Jersey. States without income tax typically have higher property taxes to compensate.

faqs.question: Why is home insurance so expensive in some states?
faqs.answer: Insurance costs are significantly higher in states prone to natural disasters. Florida averages about 1.05% of home value due to hurricane risk. Oklahoma and Louisiana are high due to tornado and hurricane exposure. Hawaii, Utah, and Oregon have the lowest rates.

faqs.question: Does this include taxes and insurance?
faqs.answer: Yes. After you select a state, property taxes and home insurance are estimated automatically based on state averages and the home price. These are added to the principal and interest payment to show the true monthly cost. You can also adjust both values manually.

faqs.question: What is an amortization schedule?
faqs.answer: An amortization schedule shows how each monthly payment is split between principal and interest over the life of the loan. Early payments are mostly interest; later payments are mostly principal.

faqs.question: What is an Open Graph preview?
faqs.answer: An Open Graph preview shows how your website looks when shared on Facebook, LinkedIn, and other social platforms. It uses your site's og: meta tags to display the title, description, image, and URL.

faqs.question: How do I use the OG preview?
faqs.answer: Enter your website URL. The tool fetches and parses the Open Graph tags, then shows previews of how it will look when shared on Facebook and Twitter.

faqs.question: Why does my preview look wrong?
faqs.answer: Check that your site has the correct og:title, og:description, og:image, and og:url tags. Images should be at least 1200x630 pixels. Some platforms cache previews, so it may take time to update.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Facebook and Twitter previews?
faqs.answer: Facebook uses Open Graph tags, while Twitter uses Twitter Card tags (falling back to Open Graph if available). The layouts and designs are also slightly different.

faqs.question: Can I preview the OG tags of a specific page?
faqs.answer: Yes. Enter any URL and the tool will fetch that page's OG tags and display the preview.

faqs.question: Are the previews accurate?

faqs.question: How do I calculate a percentage of a number?
faqs.answer: Multiply the number by the percentage divided by 100. For example, 25% of 200 = 200 * (25/100) = 50.

faqs.question: How do I calculate percentage change?
faqs.answer: Percentage change = ((new value - old value) / old value) * 100. A change from 80 to 100 is ((100-80)/80) * 100 = a 25% increase.

faqs.question: What's the difference between percentage and percentage points?
faqs.answer: A change from 10% to 15% is a 5 percentage point increase, but a 50% percentage increase. Percentage points measure absolute differences; percentages measure relative change.

faqs.question: What is the 4% rule?
faqs.answer: The 4% rule suggests you can withdraw 4% of your retirement savings per year without running out of money over 30 years. It's based on research using historical market returns. Adjust for inflation to maintain purchasing power.

faqs.question: How much do I need to retire?
faqs.answer: Multiply your annual expenses by 25 (based on the 4% rule). If you need $50,000 per year, aim for $1.25 million. This includes Social Security and pensions as income sources.

faqs.question: How does Social Security affect retirement?
faqs.answer: Social Security replaces about 40% of pre-retirement income. Higher earners get a lower replacement percentage. Claim at 67 (full retirement age), or wait until 70 to increase payments by 8%/year.

faqs.question: How aggressive should I invest?
faqs.answer: A rule of thumb: stock percentage = 110 - your age. At 30: 80% stocks. At 60: 50% stocks. Reduce risk as you approach retirement. But adjust based on your risk tolerance and time horizon.

faqs.question: How do I convert annual salary to hourly?
faqs.answer: Divide the annual salary by the number of hours worked per year. For a standard 40-hour work week, 52 weeks: $65,000 / 2,080 hours = $31.25/hour.

faqs.question: How do I convert hourly to annual salary?
faqs.answer: Multiply the hourly rate by the hours per week, then by the weeks per year. $20/hour * 40 hours * 52 weeks = $41,600/year.

faqs.question: What if I have paid vacation?
faqs.answer: If your employer provides paid vacation, keep weeks per year at 52 - you still get paid for those weeks. Only reduce the number if you have unpaid time off.

faqs.question: How does compound interest affect savings?
faqs.answer: Compound interest accrues on both your principal and accumulated interest. Compounding monthly vs. annually produces slightly higher returns. The difference grows with time and rate.

faqs.question: How do regular deposits affect growth?
faqs.answer: Regular deposits significantly increase the final balance through compounding. Depositing $200/month at a 5% annual return for 10 years = about $31,000 - you contribute $24,000 and interest contributes $7,000.

faqs.question: What's the difference between savings and money market accounts?
faqs.answer: Savings accounts offer a fixed rate and simple access. Money market accounts typically offer higher rates but require higher minimum balances and may offer check-writing privileges. Both are FDIC-insured.

faqs.question: How does inflation affect my savings?
faqs.answer: Inflation erodes purchasing power. 3% inflation reduces purchasing power by 26% over 10 years. Always compare your savings rate to inflation - if the rate is below inflation, your money is losing real value.

faqs.question: Can I choose a custom short link?
faqs.answer: Yes. Enter an alias in the optional custom field and the tool will request that short code from is.gd. Whether the custom code is available depends on the provider's service status and usage limits.

faqs.question: Are my links tracked or logged?
faqs.answer: No. The tool only forwards your URL to the shortening service and returns the short link. This site performs no statistics, tracking, or storage.

faqs.question: Do short links expire?
faqs.answer: Links generated by is.gd and TinyURL are permanent and don't expire, unless the target page is removed.

faqs.question: Why was my short link generated by TinyURL?
faqs.answer: The tool prefers is.gd (which supports structured errors and custom short links). When is.gd is rate-limited or unavailable, it automatically falls back to TinyURL so you still get a working short link.

faqs.question: What URLs are supported?
faqs.answer: Any public http or https link. Private addresses or localhost will be rejected by the shortening services.

faqs.question: Why doesn't my short link open?
faqs.answer: Short links are hosted by third-party services is.gd and TinyURL, and these domains may not be accessible from some networks (such as mainland China). The short link itself is valid—if it doesn't open, switch to a network that can reach these domains.

faqs.answer: A URL slug is the text portion of a URL that identifies a specific page. It should be readable, SEO-friendly, and contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens. For example: "my-blog-post".

faqs.answer: Yes. Descriptive slugs help search engines understand page content. They also make it easier for users to predict what a link contains. Good slugs can improve search engine rankings and click-through rates.

faqs.question: What characters should I use in a slug?
faqs.answer: Use lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens. Avoid spaces, uppercase, special characters, and consecutive hyphens. Keep slugs short but descriptive.

faqs.question: How does the U.S. Navy method work?
faqs.answer: The U.S. Navy body fat formula uses circumference measurements (waist, neck, and hips for women) combined with height to estimate body fat percentage. It is fairly accurate for most people and requires no specialized equipment.

faqs.question: How do I measure correctly?
faqs.answer: Waist: measure at the narrowest point (at navel level for men). Neck: measure below the larynx. Hips (women only): measure at the widest point. Use a soft tape measure, keep it snug but not compressed, and measure in the morning.

faqs.question: What is a healthy body fat percentage?
faqs.answer: Men: 10-20% is considered fit, 6-13% for athletes. Women: 18-28% is fit, 14-20% for athletes. Essential fat minimums are about 2-5% for men and 10-13% for women.

faqs.question: How are daily calories calculated?
faqs.answer: This calculator uses the Mifflin-St Jeor equation to calculate your Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR), then multiplies it by an activity factor to get your Total Daily Energy Expenditure (TDEE). The Mifflin-St Jeor equation is considered the most accurate equation for most people.

faqs.question: How many calories should I eat to lose weight?
faqs.answer: Reducing your daily intake by 500 calories leads to roughly 1 pound of weight loss per week. A 250-calorie reduction is about 0.5 pounds per week. Don't go below 1,200 calories for women or 1,500 calories for men without medical supervision.

faqs.question: What is the difference between BMR and TDEE?
faqs.answer: BMR (Basal Metabolic Rate) is the calories your body burns at complete rest - just to stay alive. TDEE (Total Daily Energy Expenditure) is BMR plus the calories burned through activity. TDEE is what you actually need to eat to maintain your weight.

faqs.question: Is the calorie calculator accurate?
faqs.answer: Calorie calculators provide estimates, not exact numbers. Individual metabolic differences range from +/- 10-15%. Use the result as a starting point, track your weight for 2-3 weeks, then adjust up or down based on actual results.

faqs.question: How do I calculate how much concrete I need?
faqs.answer: Measure the length, width, and depth (thickness) of the project area. Multiply these three dimensions together to get the volume. For a rectangular slab, use length x width x depth. For a cylinder, use pi x radius squared x height. Always add 5-10% extra material for waste, spillage, and uneven subgrade.

faqs.question: How many bags of concrete do I need?
faqs.answer: First calculate the total cubic feet required. Then divide by the bag yield: a 40-lb bag covers 0.30 cubic feet, a 60-lb bag covers 0.45 cubic feet, and an 80-lb bag covers 0.60 cubic feet. For example, a 10x10 foot slab 4 inches thick needs about 33.3 cubic feet, about 56 bags of 80-lb concrete mix.

faqs.question: How thick should a concrete slab be?
faqs.answer: Sidewalks and patios typically require 4 inches of concrete. Driveways and garage floors should be 6 inches thick. Foundation walls are usually 8 inches, and foundations or footings are typically 12 inches thick. Heavier loads and vehicle traffic require thicker slabs.

faqs.question: What is the difference between cubic yards and cubic feet of concrete?
faqs.answer: 1 cubic yard equals 27 cubic feet. Ready-mix concrete bought from a truck is usually sold by the cubic yard, while bagged concrete is measured in cubic feet. To convert cubic feet to cubic yards, divide by 27. For example, 81 cubic feet equals 3 cubic yards.

faqs.question: How much does a yard of concrete cost?
faqs.answer: Ready-mix concrete typically costs $120 to $200 per cubic yard delivered, depending on your location, mix type, and delivery distance. Orders below 5-10 yards may incur a short-load fee. Specialty mixes, fiber reinforcement, or accelerated curing may add $10-30 per yard.

faqs.question: Should I add extra concrete for waste?
faqs.answer: Yes, always add a 5-10% waste factor to your calculated volume. This accounts for spillage, uneven subgrade, form irregularities, and over-excavation. For complex shapes like stairs or irregular forms, consider adding 10-15% extra. It's always better to have extra concrete than not enough during a pour.

faqs.question: When should I use bagged vs. ready-mix concrete?
faqs.answer: Bagged concrete is best for small projects under 1 cubic yard, such as setting fence posts, small pads, or repairs. For projects over 1-2 cubic yards, ready-mix delivery is more cost-effective and practical. Mixing more than 40-50 bags by hand is very labor-intensive.

whatIs.title: How to Use the Concrete Calculator
whatIs.content: This calculator helps you estimate the amount of concrete needed for any project. Choose the shape you're pouring, enter the dimensions, and get instant results in cubic yards, cubic feet, and cubic meters. You can add multiple sections to calculate combined totals for complex projects.

howTo.title: Supported Shapes
howTo.content: Slab/Square: for patios, sidewalks, driveways, and garage floors. Enter length, width, and depth. Cylinder/Column: for round columns, piers, sonotubes, and post holes. Enter diameter and height. Wall/Footing: for foundation walls, retaining walls, and footings. Enter length, height, and wall thickness. Stairs: for concrete steps. Enter the number of steps, riser height, tread width, and total stair width.

tips.title: Tips
tips.content: Always order 5-10% more concrete than your calculations to account for waste and uneven ground. For ready-mix deliveries, most companies have a 1 cubic yard minimum, and small orders may incur a short-load fee. One 80-lb bag of premix concrete yields about 0.6 cubic feet of cured concrete.

faqs.question: What is the avalanche method?
faqs.answer: The avalanche method pays off the debt with the highest interest rate first while making minimum payments on other debts. This mathematically saves the most interest but may take longer to see progress.

faqs.question: What is the snowball method?
faqs.answer: The snowball method pays off the debt with the smallest balance first while making minimum payments on other debts. This provides quick wins and motivation but costs more in interest than the avalanche method.

faqs.question: Should I consolidate my debt?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you can consolidate at a lower rate (personal loan, balance transfer card). Balance transfer cards offer 0% APR for 12-18 months but charge transfer fees of 3-5%. It only works if you can pay it off before the promo period ends.

faqs.question: Where should extra payments go?
faqs.answer: Always apply extra payments to the principal - not to future payments. This immediately reduces the balance and saves interest. Specify 'apply to principal' when making payments.

faqs.question: How do I calculate a discount?
faqs.answer: Discount = Original Price * (Discount Percentage / 100). Final Price = Original Price - Discount. For example, 25% off a $100 item: discount = 100 * (25/100) = $25, final price = 100 - 25 = $75.

faqs.question: How do consecutive discounts work?
faqs.answer: Consecutive discounts are not simply added. 50% plus 30% is not an 80% discount. After the first discount, the second discount applies to the reduced price. $100: after 50% = $50, then 30% of $50 = $15, final = $35 (65% off total).

faqs.question: How do I reverse-calculate the original price from the final price?
faqs.answer: Original Price = Final Price / (1 - Discount Rate). If an item sold for $75 at 25% off: original price = 75 / (1 - 0.25) = 75 / 0.75 = $100.

faqs.question: What is a kilowatt-hour (kWh)?
faqs.answer: A kilowatt-hour is a unit of energy - running a 1,000-watt appliance for one hour. A 100-watt light bulb running for 10 hours uses 1 kWh. Electricity is billed per kWh.

faqs.question: How do I find my electricity rate?
faqs.answer: Check your electricity bill - it shows the cents per kWh rate. The U.S. average is 17 cents/kWh. Rates vary by state, time of day, and usage.

faqs.question: How much electricity do appliances use?
faqs.answer: Central air conditioning: 3,000-5,000 watts. Refrigerator: 150-400 watts. LED lights: 10-15 watts. Microwave: 1,000 watts. Water heater: 4,500 watts. Use watts * hours / 1,000 = kWh.

faqs.question: How can I lower my electricity bill?
faqs.answer: Switch to LED lights (save 75%). Seal duct leaks. Use a programmable thermostat. Run appliances during off-peak hours. Upgrade to energy-efficient appliances. These can reduce your bill by 20-30%.

faqs.question: How do I convert hourly wage to annual salary?
faqs.answer: Multiply the hourly rate by hours per week, then by weeks per year. $20/hour * 40 hours * 52 weeks = $41,600/year.

faqs.question: How do I convert annual salary to hourly wage?
faqs.answer: Divide the annual salary by the number of work hours per year. Standard 40-hour work week, 52 weeks: $65,000 / 2,080 hours = $31.25/hour.

faqs.question: Are paid holidays included in the calculation?
faqs.answer: If you have paid vacation, use 52 weeks - you're still paid for those weeks. If you only have unpaid vacation, reduce the number of weeks. Most full-time jobs include paid vacation.

faqs.question: How do taxes affect the conversion?
faqs.answer: These calculations are pre-tax (gross income). After-tax (net income) depends on your tax bracket, deductions, and credits. Use a paycheck calculator to estimate after-tax income.

faqs.question: How do tax brackets work?
faqs.answer: Tax brackets are marginal - only the income within each bracket is taxed at that rate. Being 'in the 24% bracket' does not mean all your income is taxed at 24%. The first $11,925 (single) is taxed at 10%, the next portion at 12%, and so on.

faqs.question: What is the difference between marginal and effective tax rates?
faqs.answer: Your marginal tax rate is the bracket your last dollar falls into. Your effective tax rate is total tax divided by total income. Someone earning $85,000 (single) has a marginal rate of 22% but an effective rate of only about 14%.

faqs.question: Should I take the standard deduction or itemize?
faqs.answer: Take whichever is larger. The 2026 standard deduction is $15,700 (single) or $31,400 (married). Only itemize if your deductible expenses (mortgage interest, state/local taxes up to $10,000, charitable donations) exceed the standard deduction.

faqs.question: Where does the CPI data come from?
faqs.answer: This calculator uses annual averages of the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) published by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. CPI data goes back to 1913 and is updated each year. The reference period is 1982-84 = 100.

faqs.question: What is the average inflation rate in the U.S.?
faqs.answer: From 1913 to 2025, the average annual inflation rate in the U.S. has been about 3.2%. But this varies by decade: the 1970s averaged over 7%, while the 2010s averaged under 2%. Recent years saw a spike reaching 8% in 2022, then cooling to about 2.5% in 2025.

faqs.question: How does inflation affect purchasing power?
faqs.answer: Inflation reduces what each dollar can buy. If inflation is 3% per year, $100 today buys only $97 worth of goods next year. Over 25 years at 3%, $100 loses more than half its purchasing power - you would need about $209 to buy what $100 bought 25 years ago.

faqs.question: Why did inflation spike in 2021-2022?
faqs.answer: The 2021-2022 inflation spike was driven by pandemic-era stimulus spending, supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, and energy price increases following geopolitical events. CPI rose 4.7% in 2021 and 8.0% in 2022 - the highest since 1981.

faqs.question: Is CPI the only way to measure inflation?
faqs.answer: No. Other measures include the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index (the Fed's preferred gauge), the Producer Price Index (PPI), and core CPI (excluding volatile food and energy prices). Each captures a different aspect of price changes.

faqs.question: How is the inflation adjustment calculated?
faqs.answer: The formula is: Adjusted Amount = Original Amount * (Target Year CPI / Original Year CPI). For example, $100 in 1990 with a CPI of 130.7, adjusted to 2025 with a CPI of 321.4: $100 * (321.4 / 130.7) = $245.83.

faqs.question: What is the difference between simple and compound interest?
faqs.answer: Simple interest is calculated only on the original principal: I = P * r * t. Compound interest is calculated on the principal plus accumulated interest, so you earn 'interest on interest'. Over time, compounding grows faster.

faqs.question: What is APY?
faqs.answer: APY (Annual Percentage Yield) is the effective annual rate when compounding is considered. A 5% rate compounded monthly has an APY of 5.12%. APY lets you compare accounts with different compounding frequencies.

faqs.question: How often should interest be compounded?
faqs.answer: More frequent compounding earns slightly more. $10,000 at 5% for 10 years: monthly compounding = $16,470, annual compounding = $16,289 - a difference of $181. Daily compounding adds even less on top of monthly.

faqs.question: What are macronutrients?
faqs.answer: Macronutrients (macros) are the three main nutrients that provide calories: protein (4 cal/g), carbohydrates (4 cal/g), and fat (9 cal/g). Tracking macros helps you control body composition, not just total calories.

faqs.question: How much protein do I need?
faqs.answer: For muscle gain: 0.7-1.0 grams per pound of body weight. For maintenance: 0.5-0.7 grams per pound. For fat loss: 0.8-1.2 grams per pound (higher protein preserves muscle during a calorie deficit).

faqs.question: Which macro split should I choose?
faqs.answer: Balanced (30/40/30) works for most people. High protein (40/35/25) is best for muscle gain. Low carb (40/20/40) suits people who feel better on fewer carbs. Keto (30/5/65) is for people adapted to ketosis, with very low carbs.

faqs.question: Do I need to hit my macros exactly?
faqs.answer: No. Hit your protein target within +/- 5 grams (most important), and carbs and fat can be flexible. Hitting your calorie target matters most, followed by protein. Carbs and fat can flex based on preference.

metadata.title: Medicaid Work Requirement Calculator
metadata.description: Check if you must meet the new 80-hour work requirement, whether you qualify for an exemption, and what to do next.

faqs.question: What is the Medicaid work requirement?
faqs.answer: Under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA), adults aged 19-64 who joined Medicaid through the ACA expansion must complete 80 hours of qualifying activities per month, such as employment, job training, education, or community service. This takes effect January 1, 2027 for most states, though some states (like Nebraska) are implementing it early. Non-compliance can result in losing Medicaid coverage.

faqs.question: Who is exempt from the Medicaid work requirement?
faqs.answer: Mandatory exemptions include: people who are pregnant, parents/caretakers of children 13 or younger, caretakers of people with disabilities, people who are blind, disabled, or medically frail (including those with substance use disorders, serious mental illness, or complex conditions), disabled veterans, American Indians/Alaska Natives, former foster youth under 26, people in substance abuse treatment programs, people already meeting TANF or SNAP work requirements, people currently incarcerated or released within 90 days, and certain Medicare beneficiaries. Additionally, earning at least $580 per month from employment satisfies the requirement through the income-based alternative.

faqs.question: What activities count toward the 80 hours?
faqs.answer: Qualifying activities include: paid employment (part-time or full-time), job training or workforce development programs, enrollment in higher education or vocational/technical education (at least half-time), community service or volunteer activities, and participation in work programs. There is also an income-based alternative: earning at least $580 per month satisfies the requirement regardless of hours. Caring for a child under 13 or a disabled family member makes you exempt. 80 hours per month is roughly equivalent to 20 hours per week.

faqs.question: What happens if I don't meet the 80 hours?
faqs.answer: If your state cannot verify your compliance, you'll receive a notice and have a 30-day cure period to prove compliance or request an exemption. If you don't respond within 30 days, you'll be disenrolled from Medicaid. To restore coverage, you must reapply from scratch. Importantly, people who lose Medicaid due to work requirement non-compliance are also ineligible for ACA marketplace premium tax credits, meaning you also can't get subsidized health insurance through Healthcare.gov.

faqs.question: When does this take effect?
faqs.answer: The federal mandate takes effect January 1, 2027. However, states can implement the requirement early. Nebraska began enforcement on May 1, 2026. States are required to begin notifying beneficiaries between June 30 and August 31, 2026. HHS must release the full interim final rule by June 1, 2026.

faqs.question: Does this apply in every state?
faqs.answer: It applies to all states that have expanded Medicaid (40 states plus Washington, D.C.). The 10 states that have not expanded Medicaid (Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Kansas, Mississippi, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Wisconsin, Wyoming) are not directly affected because they have no Medicaid expansion population. States cannot waive this requirement after January 1, 2027.

faqs.question: Will I permanently lose health insurance?
faqs.answer: You will lose Medicaid and must reapply. There is no automatic reinstatement. Additionally, the law bars people disenrolled for non-compliance from receiving ACA marketplace premium tax credits, meaning you may not be able to get affordable health insurance through any subsidized program until you regain Medicaid eligibility. This makes compliance or requesting an exemption extremely important.

faqs.question: How do I report my hours?
faqs.answer: States must first try to verify your compliance through automatic data matching (wage records, TANF/SNAP records, education enrollment). If your hours can't be verified automatically, you may need to self-report. Your state Medicaid office will provide specific reporting instructions. States verify compliance at least every 6 months.

faqs.question: Does part-time work count?
faqs.answer: Yes. Any paid employment counts toward the 80 monthly hours, including part-time work. If you work 20 hours a week, you meet the requirement. There is no minimum wage or income threshold - only the hours matter.

faqs.question: What if I'm between jobs?
faqs.answer: If you're temporarily unemployed, you can meet the requirement through job training, education (at least half-time), community service, or volunteer activities. You can combine different qualifying activities to reach 80 hours. If you've recently been released from incarceration (within 90 days), you're temporarily exempt.

whatIs.title: Understanding the Medicaid Work Requirement
whatIs.content: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) was signed into law in 2025 and adds new work requirements for adults who joined Medicaid through the ACA expansion. Starting January 1, 2027, you must complete 80 hours of qualifying activities per month to keep your Medicaid coverage. Some states are implementing this early - Nebraska began enforcement in May 2026.

howTo.title: Who Is Affected and Qualifying Activities
howTo.content: This requirement applies to adults aged 19-64 who joined Medicaid through the expansion program (typically people with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level). About 18.5 million people nationwide are enrolled in expansion Medicaid. You can satisfy the 80-hour requirement through any combination of: paid employment (any job, part-time or full-time), job training (workforce development programs, apprenticeships, or vocational training), higher education or vocational/technical education (must be enrolled at least half-time), and community service (volunteering at nonprofits, faith-based organizations, or government programs). There is also an income-based alternative: earning at least $580 per month (80 hours at the federal minimum wage of $7.25/hour) satisfies the requirement regardless of actual hours worked.

tips.title: Exemptions and Consequences of Non-Compliance
tips.content: Many people are exempt and don't need to meet the 80-hour requirement. Exemptions include: people who are pregnant or within 12 months postpartum, parents or caretakers of children 13 or younger, caretakers of family members with disabilities, people with disabilities (physical, intellectual, or developmental), people with substance use disorders, serious mental illness, or complex conditions, disabled veterans, American Indians and Alaska Natives, former foster youth under 26, people in substance abuse treatment programs, people already meeting TANF or SNAP work requirements, people currently incarcerated or released within the past 90 days, and certain Medicare beneficiaries. If your state can't verify that you meet the 80-hour requirement, you'll receive a notice. You then have 30 days to prove compliance or request an exemption. If you don't respond, you'll be disenrolled from Medicaid and must reapply from scratch to restore coverage. Importantly, if you lose Medicaid for failing the work requirement, you'll also be barred from premium tax credits for ACA marketplace insurance (Healthcare.gov).

faqs.question: What is the OBBA bill?
faqs.answer: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBA) is a proposed tax legislation that includes tip tax exemptions, overtime pay exemptions, a senior citizen deduction, and an auto loan interest deduction. It aims to reduce the tax burden on working Americans and seniors.

faqs.question: How does the tip tax exemption work?
faqs.answer: OBBA allows service workers to exclude up to $30,000 of tip income (single) or $60,000 (married filing jointly) from taxable income. This applies to workers who receive tips - servers, bartenders, hotel staff.

faqs.question: What is the senior citizen deduction?
faqs.answer: Taxpayers 65 and older can claim an additional standard deduction of up to $6,000 (single) or $12,000 (married filing jointly). This reduces taxable income, directly lowering the tax bill.

faqs.question: What is the auto loan interest deduction?
faqs.answer: OBBA allows deducting up to $10,000 of auto loan interest (available to taxpayers with AGI below $100,000). This applies to individuals purchasing new cars.

metadata.title: Paint Calculator
metadata.description: Estimate the amount of paint needed based on wall area, door/window area, number of coats, and coverage.

faqs.question: How much paint do I need for a 12x12 room?
faqs.answer: A 12x12 room with 8-foot ceilings has about 384 square feet of wall area. Subtract a door (about 21 sq ft) and a window (about 15 sq ft), and you have roughly 348 square feet of paintable surface. With 2 coats and standard coverage of 350 sq ft per gallon, you'll need about 2 gallons of paint.

faqs.question: How many square feet does a gallon of paint cover?
faqs.answer: A gallon of interior latex paint typically covers 350-400 square feet per coat on smooth surfaces. Textured walls, unpainted drywall, or porous surfaces can reduce coverage to 200-300 sq ft per gallon. Premium paints sometimes offer higher coverage, around 400+ sq ft per gallon.

faqs.question: Should I buy gallons or quarts of paint?
faqs.answer: Gallons are more cost-effective per unit volume. Quarts typically cost about 30% of the gallon price but only contain 25% of the paint. Buy gallons for large areas, and quarts only for small touch-ups or accent walls under 100 square feet. This calculator shows the best combination.

faqs.question: How do I calculate paint for a room with vaulted ceilings?
faqs.answer: For vaulted or cathedral ceilings, use this calculator's manual mode. Measure each wall separately, calculate the area of triangular or trapezoid walls (base * average height), then enter the total wall area. Remember to subtract doors and windows as usual.

faqs.question: Do I need to calculate primer separately?
faqs.answer: Yes. Primer coverage differs from paint, typically 200-300 square feet per gallon. If painting over dark colors, new drywall, or stained surfaces, add a primer coat before the paint coats. Some paint-and-primer combo products may skip this step, but separate primer works better on problem surfaces.

faqs.question: How much extra paint should I buy?
faqs.answer: Buy 10-15% extra paint to account for touch-ups, mistakes, and future repairs. This calculator rounds up to the nearest gallon, which usually provides that buffer. Store leftover paint sealed for future touch-ups, since exact color matching can be difficult later.

faqs.question: How do I estimate paint for textured walls?
faqs.answer: Textured walls absorb more paint. For light texture, reduce coverage to about 300 sq ft per gallon. For heavy texture like stucco or popcorn, use 200-250 sq ft per gallon. Adjust the coverage field in this calculator to match your wall texture for a more accurate estimate.

labels.error: Door and window area cannot be larger than wall area.

whatIs.title: How to Use the Paint Calculator
whatIs.content: Start by adding your rooms. For each room, enter the length, width, and ceiling height to automatically calculate the wall area, or switch to manual mode if you already know the total wall area. Add any doors and windows to subtract their area from the total. The calculator accounts for multiple coats and your paint coverage to give you the exact number of gallons.

howTo.title: Paint Coverage by Type
howTo.content: Flat/Matte latex: 350-400 sq ft per gallon (ceilings, low-traffic rooms). Eggshell latex: 350-400 sq ft per gallon (living rooms, bedrooms). Satin latex: 350-400 sq ft per gallon (kitchens, bathrooms, hallways). Semi-gloss latex: 350-400 sq ft per gallon (trim, doors, cabinets). High gloss: 300-350 sq ft per gallon (trim, furniture, accents). Oil/Alkyd: 350-450 sq ft per gallon (trim, cabinets, high-wear areas). Primer (latex or shellac/oil): 200-300 sq ft per gallon (new drywall, stain blocking).

tips.title: Surface Preparation Tips
tips.content: Before painting, clean the walls with a damp cloth or TSP solution to remove dust, grease, and dirt. Fill nail holes and cracks with lightweight spackle. Lightly sand glossy surfaces (120-150 grit) to help new paint adhere. Apply painter's tape to trim, ceiling edges, and any areas you want to protect. Use a stain-blocking primer on water stains, smoke damage, or when going from dark to light colors. Let the primer and each coat of paint dry completely (usually 2-4 hours for latex) before applying the next coat.

metadata.title: Paycheck Calculator
metadata.description: Estimate your take-home pay per paycheck, including federal tax, FICA, state tax, and 401k deductions.

faqs.question: Is this paycheck calculator accurate?
faqs.answer: This provides a reasonable estimate using 2026 federal tax brackets, the standard deduction, and FICA rates. Actual paychecks may differ due to local taxes, pre-tax benefits (health insurance), W-4 withholding choices, and employer-specific deductions.

faqs.question: What is FICA?
faqs.answer: FICA stands for the Federal Insurance Contributions Act. It includes Social Security tax (6.2%, up to $168,600) and Medicare tax (1.45%, plus an extra 0.9% on income over $200,000). Your employer matches these amounts.

faqs.question: Does this include state taxes?

faqs.question: How do I calculate monthly payments?
faqs.answer: Monthly payments are calculated using the standard amortization formula: M = P[r(1+r)^n]/[(1+r)^n-1], where P is the loan amount, r is the monthly interest rate, and n is the total number of payments.

faqs.question: Does a longer term mean lower payments?
faqs.answer: Yes, longer terms have lower monthly payments, but you pay more total interest. A $25,000 loan at 6.5% has a $489 monthly payment over 5 years ($4,349 interest), versus $280 over 10 years ($8,580 interest).

faqs.question: What is the difference between profit margin and markup?
faqs.answer: Profit margin is profit as a percentage of revenue (selling price). Markup is profit as a percentage of cost. $60 profit on $100 revenue is a 60% margin, but a 150% markup on a $40 cost.

faqs.question: How do I calculate profit margin?
faqs.answer: Margin = ((Revenue - Cost) / Revenue) * 100. For example, selling at $100 with a cost of $40: ((100-40)/100) * 100 = 60% margin.

faqs.question: What is a good profit margin?
faqs.answer: It varies by industry. Software: 70-90%. Retail: 2-5%. Restaurants: 3-9%. Services: 15-30%. Manufacturing: 5-10%. Compare with industry averages.

faqs.question: How do I calculate ROI?
faqs.answer: ROI = ((Final Value - Initial Investment) / Initial Investment) * 100. For example, investing $1,000 with a final value of $1,500: ROI = ((1,500 - 1,000) / 1,000) * 100 = 50%.

faqs.question: What is annualized ROI?
faqs.answer: Annualized ROI converts returns into a yearly equivalent so you can compare investments across different periods. Formula: annualized ROI = ((Final Value / Initial Value)^(1/Years) - 1) * 100.

faqs.question: What is the difference between ROI and CAGR?
faqs.answer: ROI measures the total return percentage without considering time. CAGR (Compound Annual Growth Rate) measures the annual equivalent growth rate. For multi-year investments, CAGR provides better comparability.

faqs.question: How do I calculate sales tax?
faqs.answer: Sales tax = Price * (Tax Rate / 100). For example, a $50 item at 7% tax: sales tax = 50 * (7/100) = $3.50, total = 50 + 3.50 = $53.50.

faqs.question: How do I remove sales tax from a total?
faqs.answer: Pre-tax price = Total / (1 + Tax Rate/100). If the total is $107 at 7% tax: pre-tax price = 107 / (1 + 7/100) = 107 / 1.07 = $100.

faqs.question: Which states have no sales tax?

faqs.question: What is simple interest?
faqs.answer: Simple interest is calculated only on the initial principal. Formula: Interest = Principal * Rate * Time. Unlike compound interest, your earnings don't generate earnings of their own.

faqs.question: What is the difference between simple and compound interest?
faqs.answer: Simple interest is calculated only on the principal. Compound interest is calculated on the principal and accumulated interest. $1,000 at 5% for 3 years: simple interest = $150. Compound interest = $157.63. The difference grows with time and rate.

faqs.question: Where is simple interest used?
faqs.answer: Simple interest is used for auto loans, personal loans, and short-term loans. Most mortgages and credit cards use compound interest. Always confirm which type your loan uses.

faqs.question: How do I calculate the amount due?
faqs.answer: Amount Due = Principal + Interest. Or: Amount Due = Principal * (1 + Rate * Time). $1,000 at 5% for 3 years: amount due = 1,000 * (1 + 0.05 * 3) = $1,150.

faqs.question: How do I calculate the square footage of a room?
faqs.answer: Measure the room's length and width in feet, then multiply them together. For example, a 12-foot by 10-foot room is 120 square feet. If the room is not a simple rectangle, break it into smaller rectangles, calculate each area, and add them together.

faqs.question: How many square feet are in an acre?
faqs.answer: There are exactly 43,560 square feet in an acre. To convert square feet to acres, divide the square feet by 43,560. For example, 10,000 square feet is approximately 0.23 acres.

faqs.question: How do I convert square feet to square meters?
faqs.answer: Multiply square feet by 0.0929 to get square meters. For example, 500 square feet is approximately 46.45 square meters. To convert from square meters to square feet, multiply by 10.764.

faqs.question: How do I calculate the square footage of an irregularly shaped room?
faqs.answer: Break the irregular shape into standard geometric shapes such as rectangles, triangles, or circles. Calculate the area of each shape separately, then add them all together. This calculator's L-shaped mode and room calculator make common layouts simple.

faqs.question: How much flooring do I need? Should I buy extra?
faqs.answer: Calculate the total square footage of all rooms to be floored. Standard practice is to add 10% extra material for waste from cuts, mistakes, and future repairs. For diagonal or pattern installations, add 15-20% extra material.

faqs.question: What is the difference between square feet and linear feet?
faqs.answer: Linear feet measure length in a straight line (one dimension), while square feet measure area (two dimensions). For example, a board 1 foot wide and 8 feet long is 8 linear feet and also 8 square feet. Knowing the difference matters when buying materials.

faqs.question: Is this calculator accurate?
faqs.answer: This provides a reliable estimate for W-2 employees. Actual taxes depend on many factors, including tax credits (Child Tax Credit, Earned Income Tax Credit), additional income sources, and state-specific rules. Use it as a planning tool, not a substitute for filing.

faqs.question: Why is my effective rate lower than my bracket?
faqs.answer: Tax brackets are marginal - only the income within each bracket is taxed at that rate. If you earn $85,000 (single), your first $11,925 is taxed at 10%, the next portion at 12%, and so on. Your effective rate averages all brackets, so it is always lower than your highest marginal bracket.

faqs.question: Do 401(k) contributions reduce my taxes?
faqs.answer: Yes. Traditional 401(k) contributions are pre-tax, meaning they reduce your federal and state taxable income. Contributing $10,000 to a 401(k) while in the 22% bracket saves about $2,200 in federal tax alone. This calculator accounts for 401(k) and HSA contributions.

faqs.question: Which states have no income tax?
faqs.answer: Nine states have no income tax: Alaska, Florida, Nevada, New Hampshire, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Washington, and Wyoming. However, these states typically make up the revenue through higher sales taxes, property taxes, or other fees.

faqs.question: What are FICA taxes?
faqs.answer: FICA stands for the Federal Insurance Contributions Act. It includes Social Security tax (6.2% on the first $176,100 of income) and Medicare tax (1.45% on all income, plus an additional 0.9% on income over $200,000). Your employer pays an equal amount.

faqs.question: What is TDEE?
faqs.answer: Total Daily Energy Expenditure (TDEE) is the total number of calories you burn each day, including your Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) plus all physical activity. Eating at your TDEE maintains your current weight.

faqs.question: Which formula is most accurate?
faqs.answer: Mifflin-St Jeor is considered the most accurate for most people. If you know your body fat percentage, Katch-McArdle is better because it accounts for lean body mass. Harris-Benedict is the oldest formula and tends to slightly overestimate.

faqs.question: How do I lose weight using TDEE?
faqs.answer: Subtracting 250-500 calories from your TDEE achieves steady weight loss of 0.5-1 pound per week. A 500-calorie daily deficit equals about 3,500 calories per week, roughly equal to 1 pound of fat.

faqs.question: Why is activity level so important?
faqs.answer: Activity level can change your TDEE by 40-60%. A sedentary person with a BMR of 1,700 has a TDEE of about 2,040, while a highly active person with the same BMR has a TDEE of about 2,930. Fill in your activity level honestly for accurate results.

metadata.title: Tile Calculator
metadata.description: Calculate the number of tiles needed based on area, tile size, and waste rate.

faqs.question: How do I calculate how many tiles I need?
faqs.answer: Measure the length and width of the area to get the total square footage. Divide it by the area of a single tile (in square feet) to get the base tile count. Then add 10-20% extra material for waste, cuts, and breakage based on your chosen layout pattern.

faqs.question: How much extra tile should I buy for waste?
faqs.answer: For standard straight/grid layouts, plan on 10% extra. Diagonal layouts typically need 15% waste, brick/offset patterns about 12%, and herringbone patterns about 20%. Complex room shapes with many cuts may need more. It's always better to have leftover tiles than to run out mid-project.

faqs.question: Does grout line size affect how many tiles I need?
faqs.answer: Yes. Wider grout lines slightly reduce the number of tiles needed because each tile actually covers a larger footprint (tile + half a grout line on each side). A standard 1/8-inch grout line has little effect, but larger 1/4-inch or 3/8-inch gaps can noticeably reduce tile count over large areas.

faqs.question: How do I convert tile size from inches to square feet?
faqs.answer: Multiply the tile width by the height (in inches) to get square inches, then divide by 144 (since 1 square foot = 144 square inches). For example, a 12x24-inch tile is 288 square inches / 144 = 2 square feet per tile.

faqs.question: What is the most cost-effective tile layout pattern?
faqs.answer: Straight or grid patterns are the most cost-effective because they produce the least waste (about 10%). Brick/offset adds about 12%, diagonal about 15%, and herringbone about 20%. The extra cost comes from more cuts and unusable remnants. Straight layouts also install faster, lowering labor costs.

faqs.question: How do I calculate tile for a wall or backsplash?
faqs.answer: Use the same method as for floors: measure the wall height and width to get the area, then subtract any windows, doors, or outlets. Enter these dimensions into the calculator and it will compute the tiles needed. For backsplashes, measure from the countertop to the bottom of the upper cabinets.

faqs.question: Should I round up tiles or boxes?
faqs.answer: Always round up. You can't buy partial tiles or partial boxes. This calculator automatically rounds up the number of tiles and boxes. Having a few extra tiles for future repairs is better than running out mid-installation.

whatIs.title: How to Use the Tile Calculator

howTo.content: Step 1: Enter your area dimensions - measure the length and width of the area you're tiling. You can enter measurements in feet and inches, or switch to metric for projects using meters. Step 2: Choose your tile size - select from common tile sizes like 12x12, 12x24, or 24x24 inches, or enter a custom tile size. The calculator accounts for grout line width when determining how many tiles fit in your space. Step 3: Choose a layout pattern - different layout patterns require different amounts of waste material due to cuts. Straight/grid is the most efficient, while herringbone requires the most extra material. The calculator automatically adjusts the waste percentage based on your chosen pattern, or you can set a custom waste percentage. Step 4: View results and cost - the results section shows the total number of tiles needed (with and without waste), the number of boxes to purchase, and the estimated total cost based on the price you entered.

tips.content: Straight/Grid: about 10% waste (most efficient). Diagonal (45 degrees): about 15% waste. Herringbone: about 20% waste. Brick/Offset: about 12% waste. Complex room shapes with many cuts may need more. It's always better to have leftover tiles than to run out mid-project.

faqs.question: What is net worth?
faqs.answer: Net worth is what you own (assets) minus what you owe (liabilities). It measures financial health. A positive net worth means your assets exceed your debts. A negative net worth means your debts exceed your assets.

faqs.question: What counts as an asset?
faqs.answer: Assets include: cash and savings accounts, investments (stocks, bonds, retirement accounts), real estate market value, vehicle value, personal property (jewelry, art), and retirement accounts.

faqs.question: What counts as a liability?
faqs.answer: Liabilities include: mortgage balances, car loans, student loans, credit card debt, medical debt, personal loans, and any other money you owe.

faqs.question: How often should I calculate my net worth?
faqs.answer: Track progress quarterly or semiannually. More frequent tracking can cause anxiety due to market fluctuations. An annual review is sufficient for long-term planning. The trend matters more than any single number.

faqs.question: How do I calculate stock profit?
faqs.answer: Profit = (Sell Price - Buy Price) × Shares - Commission. Include all fees paid when buying and selling. This gives your net profit, not just the price difference.

faqs.question: How is the rate of return calculated?
faqs.answer: Rate of return = (Profit ÷ Total Investment) × 100. Total investment = Buy Price × Shares + Buy Commission. This shows the percentage you earned, not just the dollar amount.

faqs.question: Are dividends included in profit calculations?
faqs.answer: Not by default, but they should be. Add any dividends received during the holding period to your sell proceeds. Total profit = capital gains + dividends - fees.

faqs.question: How do taxes affect stock profits?
faqs.answer: Short-term holdings (under one year) are taxed at ordinary income rates. Long-term holdings (over one year) are taxed at lower capital gains rates (0%, 15%, or 20%). Hold for more than a year to minimize taxes.

faqs.answer: The debt avalanche attacks the highest-rate card first while making minimum payments on the others. It mathematically saves the most interest and pays off debt the fastest.

faqs.question: What is a balance transfer card?
faqs.answer: Balance transfer cards offer 0% APR for 12-18 months, typically charging a 3-5% fee. Savings are significant if you pay off the balance before the promo ends. If you don't, rates spike.

faqs.question: How do I stop adding to my credit card debt?
faqs.answer: Remove saved card numbers. Use cash or debit. Build an emergency fund to cover unexpected expenses. Track spending to identify triggers. Address the root cause - insufficient income or excessive spending.

faqs.question: What is PMI?
faqs.answer: Private mortgage insurance is required when your down payment is below 20%. It typically costs 0.3-1.5% of the loan amount per year. You can cancel PMI at 20% equity. Avoid it by putting down 20%.

faqs.question: How does the down payment affect interest rates?

faqs.question: Can I accept a gift as a down payment?

faqs.question: What is dividend yield?
faqs.answer: Dividend yield is the annual dividend per share divided by the stock price, expressed as a percentage. For example, a $50 stock paying a $2 annual dividend has a 4% yield (2 ÷ 50 × 100).

faqs.question: How does dividend reinvestment work?
faqs.answer: A DRIP (Dividend Reinvestment Plan) automatically uses your dividends to buy more shares, usually commission-free. This accelerates growth through compounding - your dividends buy more shares, which then generate more dividends.

faqs.question: How are dividends taxed?
faqs.answer: Qualified dividends are taxed at the lower long-term capital gains rates (0%, 15%, or 20%). Non-qualified dividends are taxed at your ordinary income rate. The stock must be held for more than 60 days during the ex-dividend period to qualify for qualified treatment.

faqs.question: Is a higher dividend yield always better?
faqs.answer: No. Unusually high yields (>8%) may signal a falling stock price or unsustainable dividends. Sustainable yields typically fall in the 2-6% range. Check the payout ratio - dividends paying out more than 60-70% of earnings may be at risk.

faqs.question: Are calorie burn estimates accurate?
faqs.answer: These are estimates based on average MET values. Individual variation exists due to differences in fitness level, efficiency, and body composition. Use these numbers to track trends rather than absolute accuracy.

metadata.title: FIRE Calculator
metadata.description: Calculate your Financial Independence number and years needed for early retirement.

faqs.question: What is the FIRE movement?
faqs.answer: FIRE (Financial Independence, Retire Early) is a movement focused on retiring before the traditional retirement age through aggressive saving and investing. A typical goal is accumulating 25 times your annual expenses in net worth.

faqs.question: What is the 4% rule?
faqs.answer: The 4% rule suggests you can withdraw 4% of your portfolio in the first year of retirement, then adjust that amount for inflation each year, with a very low probability of running out of money. 25 times your annual expenses achieves this.

faqs.question: How much do I need to FIRE?
faqs.answer: Multiply your annual expenses by 25. If you spend $40,000 per year, you need $1 million (40,000 × 25). This assumes a 4% safe withdrawal rate based on historical market returns.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Lean FIRE and Fat FIRE?

faqs.question: What is VAT?
faqs.answer: VAT (Value Added Tax) is a consumption tax levied on the value added to goods or services at each stage of the supply chain. It is ultimately borne by the end consumer, and businesses remit it to the government.

faqs.question: How do I calculate the gross price from a net price?
faqs.answer: Gross price = Net price × (1 + VAT rate). If the net price is $100 and VAT is 20%: gross price = 100 × 1.20 = $120.

faqs.question: How do I extract the net price from a gross price?
faqs.answer: Net price = Gross price ÷ (1 + VAT rate). If the gross price is $120 and VAT is 20%: net price = 120 ÷ 1.20 = $100.

faqs.question: What is the difference between VAT and GST?
faqs.answer: GST (Goods and Services Tax) is a single-stage tax collected at the point of final sale. VAT is a multi-stage tax collected at each stage of the supply chain, with credits along the way. Both function similarly but differ in structure.

faqs.question: What is the break-even point?
faqs.answer: The break-even point is where total revenue equals total costs - no profit and no loss. Above it, the business is profitable; below it, the business loses money.

faqs.question: How do I calculate the break-even point (in units)?
faqs.answer: Break-even units = Fixed costs ÷ (Selling price - Variable cost per unit). If fixed costs are $10,000, the selling price is $50, and variable costs are $30: break-even = 10,000 ÷ (50 - 30) = 500 units.

faqs.question: What is the difference between fixed and variable costs?
faqs.answer: Fixed costs do not change with production levels (rent, insurance, salaries). Variable costs change with production (raw materials, direct labor, shipping). Identifying both is essential for an accurate break-even analysis.

faqs.question: Why is break-even analysis important?
faqs.answer: It tells you how much you need to sell to start making a profit, informing pricing, cost control, and business planning. It helps evaluate the viability of new products or the impact of changes on profitability.

faqs.question: What debt-to-income (DTI) ratios do lenders use?
faqs.answer: Most lenders prefer the 28/36 rule - housing costs at no more than 28% of gross income and total debt (including housing) at no more than 36%. Some loans allow DTI up to 43-50%, but they carry more risk.

faqs.question: Should I budget for home maintenance?
faqs.answer: Yes. The rule of thumb is 1-3% of the home's value per year. A $300,000 home should have $3,000-$9,000 budgeted annually for maintenance - HVAC, roof, plumbing, and more. This is not in the mortgage payment but is essential.

faqs.question: What is the 28/36 rule?
faqs.answer: The 28/36 rule suggests your housing expenses (principal, interest, taxes, insurance) should not exceed 28% of your monthly gross income, and total debt payments (housing + car loans + credit cards, etc.) should not exceed 36%.

faqs.question: How do property taxes and insurance affect affordability?
faqs.answer: They have a significant impact. A $125,000 home pays $1,250 per year in property tax in a 1% state, versus $3,125 in a 2.5% state. This changes what you can afford. Always include taxes and insurance before calculating your home price.

faqs.question: What is APR?
faqs.answer: APR (Annual Percentage Rate) is the true annual cost of a loan expressed as a rate. It includes the interest rate plus fees (origination fees, closing costs, etc.), providing a single comparable number.

faqs.question: What is the difference between APR and the interest rate?
faqs.answer: The interest rate is your cost of borrowing. APR includes the interest rate plus loan fees (origination fees, points, mortgage insurance, closing costs). APR is always equal to or higher than the interest rate and gives the full cost picture.

faqs.question: Why is APR important for comparing loans?
faqs.answer: Lenders may offer a low rate with high fees, or a high rate with low fees. APR combines both into one number, making different loan products from different lenders truly comparable.

faqs.question: Does APR account for early repayment?
faqs.answer: No. APR assumes you hold the loan for its full term. If you pay off early or refinance, the actual cost may be higher because you pay the same fees over a shorter period.

faqs.answer: Federal loans offer income-driven repayment, Public Service Loan Forgiveness, and flexible deferment options. Private loans typically lack these protections but may offer lower rates for borrowers with good credit.

faqs.question: What is income-driven repayment (IDR)?
faqs.answer: IDR plans cap monthly payments at 10-20% of discretionary income depending on the plan. Remaining balances are forgiven after 20-25 years. There are four types: SAVE, PAYE, IBR, and ICR.

faqs.question: Should I refinance my student loans?
faqs.answer: Refinancing private loans with good credit can save on interest, but you lose protections like IDR and PSLF. If you have a stable income and do not seek forgiveness, refinancing may be worthwhile.

faqs.question: How is student loan interest calculated?
faqs.answer: Daily simple interest: daily interest = (outstanding balance × interest rate) ÷ 365. It is then capitalized (added to the principal). Federal loans do not accrue interest during school and grace periods.
